The underlying issue is WAL filling the disk, most commonly caused by a replication slot that is not advancing or by archiving failures.","likely_cause":"WAL accumulation because a replication slot is not advancing (or archiving is failing), causing old WAL segments to be retained on the data volume.","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"The only file you may delete to free space is the ballast file at /var/lib/postgresql/ballast.","evidence_ids":["RB-007#5"],"quote":"This is the only file on that volume you may delete."},{"text":"A replication slot not advancing can cause WAL to fill the disk.","evidence_ids":["RB-007#1"],"quote":"A replication slot is not advancing. A slot guarantees that WAL is kept until its consumer confirms it."}],"next_checks":["Run the slot query (SELECT … FROM pg_replication_slots) to see if any inactive slot has large retained size.","Check pg_stat_archiver for recent failures to rule out archiving issues.","Monitor /var/lib/postgresql disk usage after deleting the ballast file.","If the slot is stuck and the replica cannot be restored quickly, consider dropping the slot with DBA approval.","Request an online volume expansion in the cloud console while the above steps are performed."]}
